*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 5 of 11 closed, 4 PASSING (US-561, US-563, US-564, US-566), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560/BL-034). NEXT ITERATION PICKS UP US-565 (magnetometer acquisition, size M) per the fixed closeout order -- nothing blocks it. THEN the F-132 chrome stories (US-555..559). ***

*** US-564 CLOSED passes:true -- plausibility gate, a non-measurement must never wear data_source=real. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

*** READ THIS FIRST IF YOU ARE PICKING UP US-565: US-564 has ALREADY taken headingDeg to typed-NA whenever the magnetometer latches, so US-565's own AC ("until this lands, headingDeg must render NA via US-564's gate") is DISCHARGED. You are fixing the CHIP, not the display. And US-565's AC explicitly forbids guessing a CNTL2 value -- the gate now makes a wrong guess VISIBLE (a still-latched channel reports sensor_stale) instead of silently plausible, so characterise empirically and let the gate judge it. ***

**I INHERITED A NEARLY-COMPLETE UNCOMMITTED TREE AND THE FIRST JOB WAS FINDING WHAT WAS MISSING FROM IT, NOT REBUILDING IT.** A prior iteration had written the whole gate + 5 test files and died before committing. Running the targeted suite FIRST (91 passed) answered "how complete is this" in one command -- far faster than reading 7 files. But a green suite is not a finished story: I then walked all 7 ACs against the diff, and that is what surfaced the real gap.

**THE GAP: A 236 KB REAL-HARDWARE FIXTURE SAT ON DISK THAT NO TEST READ.** `tests/fixtures/imu_stationary_90s_2026-08-21.csv` -- 1845 genuinely captured parked-car rows off the Pi -- was ORPHANED. Meanwhile `test_check_stationaryDither_neverStale` claimed "REAL stationary-vehicle behaviour" in its docstring while feeding `math.nextafter` output. **That test could not fail: synthetic +/-1-ULP dither never repeats BY CONSTRUCTION, so it would have passed even if the chip were latched.** validationCriteria #2 ("90 s stationary -> no false positive") was being "discharged" by a test that proved nothing about hardware. That is the EXACT shape of US-560's fabricated PANEL_MODES, one sprint after we named it. **Grep for your fixtures: a fixture nothing imports is either dead weight or, worse, evidence you believe you have and do not.**

**ONE REAL CAPTURE CAN PROVE BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ILLUSTRATION.** On the SAME rows through the SAME gate: accel (1821/1845 distinct) and gyro (1845/1845) are NEVER refused, while mag (1/1845) IS. A gate that fired on nothing passes the first half; a gate that fired on everything passes the second; only a working discriminator passes both. Cheaper and stronger than any number of hand-written vectors.

**MAKE A FIXTURE SELF-VERIFYING OR ITS HEADER WILL DRIFT FROM ITS BYTES.** `test_capture_matchesItsDocumentedProvenance` re-derives the row count and per-channel distinct counts FROM THE DATA and asserts they match the CSV's own header block. Regenerate it rounded/truncated/synthetic and it goes red THERE, loudly, instead of silently weakening every assertion built on it. Rounding would have been especially fatal here -- it would MANUFACTURE the very bit-identity the gate detects.

**A MISSING FIXTURE MUST FAIL, NOT SKIP.** I made `_loadCapture()` assert rather than `pytest.skip`. A skip would quietly restore the unfalsifiable state the test exists to end, and would do it while the suite still read green. Skips are for genuinely optional environments (a live DB probe), never for the only evidence your design rests on.

**KEEP THE SYNTHETIC TEST, BUT LABEL IT.** I did not delete the ULP test -- it is a legitimate BOUNDARY pin (one representable float step is still a difference, so the check cannot be loosened into a tolerance comparison). I renamed it `test_check_syntheticUlpDither_neverStale` and its docstring now says it CANNOT witness the hardware claim and points at the real-data class. Synthetic data is fine; synthetic data WEARING A "REAL" LABEL is the defect.

**VERIFIED A PRE-EXISTING RED WAS NOT MINE INSTEAD OF ASSUMING IT.** tests/pi/obdii/ threw 18 setup ERRORs. `git status --porcelain <file>` on BOTH config.json and the test file came back EMPTY -- neither differs from HEAD -- so it reproduces on a fresh clone. Root cause is genuinely interesting: **config.json carries DOUBLE-ENCODED MOJIBAKE** (bytes C3 A2 E2 82 AC E2 80 9D where an em-dash belongs -- someone read UTF-8 as cp1252 and saved it back as UTF-8) AND the test opens it with no explicit encoding. Filed TD-086. That is the THIRD instance this iteration of ONE root cause (TD-084 = tests/ui node probe decoded with `text=True`; TD-080 = duplicated helper): **on Windows, any `open()` or `subprocess(text=True)` without explicit `encoding=` is a latent locale bug that stays invisible exactly as long as the data stays ASCII.** TD-086 recommends enabling ruff PLW1514 to kill the class permanently.

**RAN A WIDER FENCE THAN THE STORY'S OWN GATE, BECAUSE THIS TOUCHED BASE MODULES.** Story suite 95 passed; tests/pi/sensors + tests/pi/splash 481 passed/1 skipped; tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py 819 passed. The US-540-b lesson holds: `tests/ui` alone is the WRONG fence for a change to `specs/UI/dist/**` -- the deploy kit pins the shipped markup separately.

DESIGN NOTES WORTH CARRYING: enrolment in the gate is an EVIDENCE decision, never a default -- LightReader is deliberately unenrolled because a photon counter can legitimately read bit-exact zero in darkness (TD-085 records the owed measurement). Check 1 runs before check 2 and its verdict is final, so a run of zeros stays `sensor_mute` rather than being re-labelled `sensor_stale`; the two reasons name different faults. `_publishBurst` gates EVERY reading before publishing ANY, so the atomic-burst contract does not rest on the order a subclass lists its channels in.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): `python -m pytest <paths>` without `-q` prints the "N passed" summary -- no redirect dance needed. `python -m ruff check <files>` for lint (`make` is not on PATH and exits 127, which reads like a pass). PowerShell tool DOES allow `;` and `&&` chaining; the Bash tool does not. `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` heredoc works cleanly in Bash. **Editing a long JSON value with the Edit tool: my old_string ended mid-`pmSignOff` and silently DROPPED that key -- always `python -c "import json; json.load(...)"` after editing sprint.json.** Index lock CLEAR all session. Full targeted+regression run is ~15 min wall-clock on the SMB share; budget for it.
